glossary.title: How Our Stats Work
glossary.intro: We don't hide our math. Every stat on the site is explained below — what it means and exactly how we work it out. Think something is wrong, or know a better way to measure it? We'd genuinely love to hear it.

legend.title: Notation
legend.note: Brackets narrow a stat to a subset — e.g. H (rifle) = rifle hits, S (spotted) = shots while an enemy was visible. Per-round rates (KPR, DPR, APR, ADR, KAST) reuse these letters over R.

scores.title: Reading the 0–100 ratings
scores.body: Aim, Positioning, Utility and the per-stat ratings are scored out of 100 — but it's a percentile, not a percentage. 50 is an average player; 90 means you're better than ~90% of players; 20 means most players do better. This can surprise you: almost everyone counter-strafes, and the typical player does it ~81% of the time — so counter-strafing 80% of the time actually lands around 22 (just below average), even though 80% sounds high. The rating tells you where you stand versus everyone else; the raw rate is still in the match stat tables.

performance.title: Performance ratings (Aim / Positioning / Utility)
performance.body: We take the underlying stats for each area, score each one as a percentile against every other player (using players with at least 30 rounds), then average them into a single 0–100 rating per area. Aim grows richer over time: stats like crosshair placement and time-to-damage fold in as more demos are parsed.

consistency.title: Consistency
consistency.body: Each match gets one overall score — your Aim, Positioning and Utility for that match, combined. The chart plots it over your recent matches, and the consistency number reflects how little it swings: a flatter line scores higher.

focus.title: Focus areas
focus.body: Your three lowest-scoring underlying stats — the spots with the most room to grow — each with a short tip. They update as you play.

geometry.title: Line of sight & the 3D model
geometry.body: On maps we have a collision mesh for, we load the map's 3D geometry and ray-cast between players to confirm a real line of sight. So 'spotted', crosshair placement, time-to-damage and engagement stats only count when you could actually see the enemy — not through smoke or a wall. On maps without a mesh we fall back to the game's spotted flag and label those stats 'Estimated'.

glossary.scale_legend: — rough scale of what subpar to elite looks like for each stat
glossary.scale_hint: Rough subpar → elite scale (estimated, not from your data yet)
glossary.mesh_help: Uses the map's 3D collision mesh. We ray-cast a line of sight between the two players, so only real sightlines count — spots through smoke, walls or thin gaps are filtered out. Needs the map geometry to be available; falls back to the raw engine data when it isn't.
glossary.mesh_legend: marks a stat validated against the map's 3D collision mesh (line-of-sight checked)
glossary.mesh_coverage_note: Mesh-validated stats (marked above) only get their line-of-sight check on maps we have a collision mesh for. Official maps without a mesh fall back to the raw engine spotted flag. Workshop maps are not listed here.

aim.label: Aim
aim.description: Your shooting — accuracy, headshots, and how quickly/cleanly you hit visible enemies. Scored 0–100 as the average percentile of those aim stats vs all players (50 = average).

positioning.label: Positioning
positioning.description: Where you fight — surviving rounds, dying near teammates so you get traded, and contributing every round (KAST). Scored 0–100 as the average percentile of those stats vs all players (50 = average).

utility.label: Utility
utility.description: Grenade impact — flash assists, how much you blind enemies, and HE/molotov damage per utility. Scored 0–100 as the average percentile vs all players. Provisional: utility doesn't yet cleanly separate skill on our data.

consistency.label: Consistency
consistency.description: Each match gets one overall score (Aim, Positioning and Utility combined). Consistency reflects how little that score swings match to match — less swing is better.

accuracy.label: Accuracy
accuracy.description: Bullets that hit an enemy, out of every bullet you fired.

accuracy_spotted.label: Spotted Accuracy
accuracy_spotted.description: Your hit rate while an enemy was actually visible — spam through smoke or walls doesn't count.

crosshair_placement.label: Crosshair Placement
crosshair_placement.description: How close your crosshair already is to the enemy when they appear. A smaller angle means less to move before firing.

time_to_damage.label: Time to Damage
time_to_damage.description: How fast you deal damage after first seeing an enemy — a proxy for reaction speed.

counter_strafing.label: Counter-Strafing
counter_strafing.description: How often you fully stop moving before firing. Shots while moving are wildly inaccurate.

first_bullet.label: First Bullet
first_bullet.description: How often your opening shot of a duel hits — the shot that decides most fights.

tracking.label: Tracking
tracking.description: While engaging a visible enemy, how much of the time your crosshair stays on them.

flash_assists.label: Flash Assists
flash_assists.description: Kills your flash set up — you blinded an enemy and a teammate killed them shortly after.

flash_blind.label: Flash Effectiveness
flash_blind.description: How much enemy blindness your flashes actually cause — rewards pop-flashes, not flashes thrown over heads.

util_efficiency.label: Utility Damage
util_efficiency.description: Damage dealt per HE/molotov you throw — rewards landing utility, not just buying them.

trade_kills.label: Trade Kills
trade_kills.description: Kills where you avenged a teammate who had just died (within a few seconds).

traded.label: Traded Deaths
traded.description: How often, when you die, a teammate trades the kill back right after — a sign of fighting near your team.

opening.label: Opening Duels
opening.description: Your win rate in the first duel of the round — first kill versus first death.

opening_attempts.label: Opening Attempts
opening_attempts.description: How often you take the round's first duel.

buy_pistol.label: Pistol Round
buy_pistol.description: The first round of each half — everyone starts with only a pistol and limited cash.

buy_eco.label: Eco
buy_eco.description: An 'eco' round: the team deliberately saves, buying little or nothing (under $5,000 total).

buy_force.label: Force Buy
buy_force.description: A force / half buy: the team spends most of its money but can't afford a full setup ($5,000–$20,000).

buy_full.label: Full Buy
buy_full.description: A full buy: rifles, armour and utility for the whole team (over $20,000).

buy_win_rate.label: Buy Win %
buy_win_rate.description: How often the team wins rounds on a given buy type — useful for spotting weak eco or anti-eco rounds.

man_advantage.label: Man Advantage %
man_advantage.description: How often you win the round after winning the opening duel — closing out the rounds you start ahead in.

man_disadvantage.label: Man Disadvantage %
man_disadvantage.description: How often you still win the round after losing the opening duel — clawing back rounds you start behind in.

net_trade.label: Net Trade
net_trade.description: Your trade kills minus your own deaths that a teammate failed to trade back — positive means you trade more than you cost the team.

trade_kill_opportunities.label: Trade Kill Opps
trade_kill_opportunities.description: How often a teammate died near you, giving you a chance to trade the killer.

trade_kill_attempts.label: Trade Kill Attempts
trade_kill_attempts.description: Of those chances, how often you actually shot at the killer.

traded_death_opportunities.label: Traded Death Opps
traded_death_opportunities.description: Your deaths where a teammate was positioned to trade you back.

traded_death_attempts.label: Traded Death Attempts
traded_death_attempts.description: Of those, how often a teammate actually shot at your killer.

traded_death_pct.label: Traded Death %
traded_death_pct.description: Share of your deaths that a teammate traded back — the same idea as Traded Deaths, shown as its own column.

total_damage.label: Total Damage
total_damage.description: Total damage you dealt to enemies across the map (ADR is this per round).

team_damage.label: Team Damage
team_damage.description: Damage you dealt to teammates (friendly fire) — lower is better.

zeus_kills.label: Zeus Kills
zeus_kills.description: Kills with the Zeus x27 taser.

multi_kill_breakdown.label: Multi-Kill Rounds (2K–5K)
multi_kill_breakdown.description: How many rounds you got exactly 2, 3, 4 or 5 kills in — the breakdown behind Multi-Kill Rounds.

flashes_thrown.label: Flashes Thrown
flashes_thrown.description: How many flashbangs you threw, effective or not.

smokes_thrown.label: Smokes Thrown
smokes_thrown.description: How many smoke grenades you threw.

round_win_pct.label: Round Win %
round_win_pct.description: Share of rounds the team won.

pistol_win_pct.label: Pistol Win %
pistol_win_pct.description: Win rate on pistol rounds — the first round of each half.

opening_win_pct.label: Opening Win % (team)
opening_win_pct.description: Team win rate in the round's first duel.

team_trade_pct.label: Trade % (team)
team_trade_pct.description: How often the team converts its trade chances into trade kills.

buy_matchup.label: Buy Matchup Win %
buy_matchup.description: Round win rate for each buy-type matchup (e.g. full-buy vs eco), not just your own buy type.

h2h_kills.label: H2H Kills
h2h_kills.description: Kills you got on a specific opponent in this match.

h2h_damage.label: H2H Damage
h2h_damage.description: Damage you dealt to a specific opponent in this match.

h2h_flashes.label: H2H Flashes
h2h_flashes.description: How many times your flashes blinded a specific opponent.

h2h_weapon_class.label: H2H by Weapon
h2h_weapon_class.description: Your kills on an opponent grouped by weapon class — rifle, pistol, sniper, and so on.

weapon_usage_pct.label: Most Used %
weapon_usage_pct.description: Share of all your kills that came with this weapon.

weapon_rating.label: Weapon Rating
weapon_rating.description: Approximate HLTV-style rating for a single weapon from its KPR, ADR and impact — directional, since there are no per-weapon deaths or KAST.

weapon_economy.description: A weapon's rating adjusted for its buy cost — about 1.0 means it performs on par for the price, higher means great value.

trade_kill_pct.label: Trade Kill %
trade_kill_pct.description: Share of your trade chances you convert — when a teammate dies near you, how often you get the avenging kill.

he_damage.label: HE Damage
he_damage.description: Damage your HE grenades deal to enemies.

molotov_damage.label: Molotov Damage
molotov_damage.description: Damage your molotovs and incendiaries deal to enemies.

he_team_damage.label: HE Team Damage
he_team_damage.description: Damage your HE grenades deal to teammates — lower is better.

enemies_flashed.label: Enemies Flashed
enemies_flashed.description: Number of enemies your flashes blinded for a meaningful amount of time (over one second).

team_flashed.label: Teammates Flashed
team_flashed.description: Number of teammates your flashes blinded — lower is better.

avg_flash_duration.label: Avg Flash Duration
avg_flash_duration.description: Average time an enemy stays blinded per flash that hits — longer pop-flashes score higher.

unused_utility.label: Unused Utility
unused_utility.description: The dollar value of grenades you were still holding when you died — utility you bought but never used.

wasted_magazine_pct.label: Wasted Mag %
wasted_magazine_pct.description: Share of your magazine left unfired when you reload — high values mean reloading too early.

elo_change.label: ELO Change
elo_change.description: How much your ELO moved after a match — scaled by the result, your performance and the series length.

elo_impact.label: ELO Impact

clutch_against.label: Against (N)
clutch_against.description: How many enemies were alive when your clutch began — the N in 1vN.

clutch_won.label: Clutch Won
clutch_won.description: You won the clutch by eliminating every remaining enemy yourself.

clutch_saved.label: Clutch Saved
clutch_saved.description: Your team won the round while you were still alive, without you having to kill everyone.

clutch_lost.label: Clutch Lost
clutch_lost.description: You died before the round was won.

clutch_win_rate.label: Clutch Win %
clutch_win_rate.description: Share of your clutches that ended in a win (saves and losses count in the denominator).

kills_in_clutch.label: Clutch Kills
kills_in_clutch.description: Kills you made while in a clutch situation.

role_entry.label: Entry (role)
role_entry.description: The player who takes the round's first duel most often (the AWPer aside).

role_support.label: Support (role)
role_support.description: The player contributing the most utility value (the AWPer and entry aside).

role_rifler.label: Rifler (role)
role_rifler.description: The default role — a rifler who isn't the AWPer, entry, or main support.

awp_share.label: AWP Share
awp_share.description: The share of your kills that came with the AWP or scoped rifle — drives the Sniper role.

entry_rate.label: Entry Rate
entry_rate.description: How often you take the round's first duel — drives the Entry role.

support_idx.label: Support Index

enemies_flashed_per.label: Enemies / Flash
enemies_flashed_per.description: Average number of enemies blinded per flash thrown — higher means more effective flashes.

opening_attempts_pct.label: Attempt Rate
opening_attempts_pct.description: Share of rounds where this player took the opening duel (first engagement of the round).

opening_success_pct.label: Win Rate
opening_success_pct.description: Share of opening duels this player won.

opening_traded_pct.label: Traded Rate

survived_pct.label: Survival Rate
survived_pct.description: Share of rounds this player survived (lived to the end of the round).

rating.label: HLTV Rating
rating.description: HLTV 2.0 overall performance rating combining kills, deaths, KAST, damage and impact. ~1.0 is average.

adr.label: ADR
adr.description: Average Damage per Round — how much damage you deal each round.

kast.label: KAST
kast.description: Percentage of rounds where you got a Kill, Assist, Survived, or were Traded.

udr.label: UDR

flash_assist_pct.description: Share of your flashes that set up a kill — you blinded an enemy and a teammate killed them shortly after.

installs.reporting_hint: Panels whose latest report is recent enough and detailed enough to count toward infrastructure and the rolling windows below. The all-time counts are not held to this — they are summed over every panel that ever reported, All time above.

totals.self_reported: All-time counts — matches, maps, players, competition — are summed across the latest report of every panel that ever sent one, including panels that have since gone quiet: a panel going dark does not un-play its matches. Infrastructure and the rolling windows count only panels heard from in the last 30 days — Current state above is how many that is — because a node torn down a year ago is not capacity, and a quiet panel's last 7 days ended whenever it stopped reporting. Panels are self-hosted and report these counts themselves; values are validated on arrival but cannot be independently verified.

totals.not_reported_hint: No panel has sent this number yet. It was added to the telemetry report after the builds currently in the fleet, so it fills in as panels update rather than meaning zero.
totals.completion_hint: Share of the matches a panel started that ended with a result rather than being abandoned part-way. Only counts matches that got as far as going live.
totals.player_base_hint: Every row is a slice of the steam ids panels have seen, and the percentage is against that top row. The rows are not stages of one another — far more steam ids have stats on a map than have ever signed in, because a panel stores a row for anyone who connects to a server.
totals.competition_hint: Match counts here overlap: a league match is played inside a tournament stage, so it is counted under both. Everything else — how many tournaments and seasons ran, who entered — counts the competition itself rather than its matches.
totals.maps_per_player_hint: Map appearances divided by the number of distinct people who have played one. A large match count with a low figure here is a small group playing a lot rather than a busy community.
totals.hosted_hint: Hosted counts only matches a panel ran itself. Imported matches come from FACEIT or CS2 match history and are listed separately.
totals.community_hint: Players counts accounts that have signed in with Steam at least once. A panel also stores a row for every steam id it has only ever seen in a lineup, a demo or a sanction — those are counted separately as Steam IDs seen.

composition.hint: Type breaks down the matches panels hosted themselves. Source spans hosted and imported both, so it adds up to more than the hosted total.

utility.title: Utility library
utility.hint: Lineups are throws somebody wrote up and kept; mined throws are grenades a demo happened to contain. The two are never added together. Archived lineups are left out of every count but their own.
utility.authors_hint: Distinct people who have written up at least one lineup, which is what separates a library one player filled in from one a community wrote.
utility.by_source_hint: In game means the practice plugin watched the throw and recorded it. Demo means it was mined out of a parsed match. Editor means somebody typed the coordinates.
utility.sessions_failed_hint: Sessions that asked for a server and never got one. A panel with no spare on-demand slots shows its shortage here.
utility.practicing_hint: Distinct players with a scored throw against a lineup, rather than everyone who joined a practice server.
utility.mastered_hint: A player and a lineup they hit often enough in a row for the panel to call it learned.
utility.verified_hint: Derived rather than awarded: a lineup verifies itself once enough separate players have mastered it in a practice server.
utility.pending_review_hint: Lineups asked to be published and still waiting on a moderator. This is a queue somebody has to work through, not a measure of use.
utility.demo_throws_hint: Grenades recovered from parsed demos. Nobody wrote these up — they are what players actually threw, and they are what the meta clusters are built from.
utility.meta_lineups_hint: Distinct spot-and-landing clusters the mined throws fall into, so the panel can offer the throw everyone runs that nobody has written up.
utility.drift_flagged_hint: Lineups a map-patch scan has ever called moved or broken, counted once each. Not how many are broken now — a repaired lineup keeps the verdict that sent it to be repaired.

players.force_name_registration_description: If forced to have player registration, the player will be required to submit a name that will be used on the platform.
players.refresh_all_description: Re-sync all player data (name, ELO, stats, sanctions) into the search index. Use this if a player looks outdated or missing in search but their profile is correct.
players.refresh_dialog_description: This will re-sync every player into the Typesense search index in batches. It runs in the background and you can watch its progress here.
players.recompute_elo_description: Wipe and rebuild every player's ELO by replaying all finished matches in order, in batches. When seasons are enabled this also rebuilds each season's ELO from the matches that fall within it. Use this after an ELO formula change or if ratings look wrong. Search results update automatically as ELO is recalculated.

players.scan_bans_description: Check every player who has been on a lineup for Steam VAC/game bans. Accounts with an active ban are auto-banned.

players.danger_zone_description: These actions are resource-intensive and run in the background across every player. They run automatically when needed — only trigger them manually if you really need to.

servers.title: Server settings

servers.plugin_runtime_warning: Switching does not move your custom plugins between addons/swiftlys2 and addons/counterstrikesharp. Servers already running keep their current image until they are recycled.

servers.reserved_disk_space_existing_gb_descript: Minimum disk space in GB required when CS2 is already installed on the node. Set to 0 to disable.

linked_accounts.faceit_test_description: Verify the Faceit API key works and whether it can download demos.

steam_presence.title: Steam presence
steam_presence.enabled_description: On by default. Friend bots watch linked players' live Steam presence and import their matches the moment they finish, instead of waiting for the hourly poll. Turn off as a kill-switch.
steam_presence.setup_step1: Dedicate a Steam account for the bot with Steam Guard enabled. Don't reuse your STEAM_USER account — that one is used elsewhere and would conflict.
steam_presence.setup_step2: Add it below. It logs in automatically; if Steam Guard prompts, a 2FA box appears on the bot — enter the code from email or the Steam app. After the first login it stays signed in and won't ask again.
steam_presence.setup_step3: Players add the bot as a Steam friend (from their settings or the profile link). Once friends, their matches import the moment they finish.
steam_presence.add_bot_description: Add a Steam account to the presence pool. Its credentials are stored to keep it signed in.
steam_presence.account_added: Bot account added — it will log in shortly
steam_presence.remove_confirm: Remove bot account {name}? Players assigned to it will be reassigned.
steam_presence.needs_2fa_email: Enter the Steam Guard code emailed to this account to finish login.
steam_presence.needs_2fa_app: Enter the Steam Guard code from the Steam mobile app for this account to finish login.
steam_presence.code_wrong: Previous code was incorrect — try again.
steam_presence.code_failed: Failed to submit Steam Guard code

steam_presence.no_bots_hint: Add a Steam account to start watching players' matches.
steam_presence.pending_tooltip: Players who were assigned a bot but haven't added it as a Steam friend yet.
steam_presence.capacity_tooltip: Total friend slots across all bots. Auto-detected from each bot's Steam level (250 + 5 × level, max 2000).
steam_presence.fetch_hint: Make sure the API is running the latest build, migrations and Hasura metadata are applied, and the web GraphQL types are regenerated (yarn codegen).

demo_settings.title: Demos
demo_settings.cloudflare_worker_description: Optional. A Cloudflare Worker in front of your Backblaze bucket serves demos, clips and media from Cloudflare's cache, so downloads don't count against the bucket's egress.
demo_settings.cloudflare_worker_not_set: Files are served straight from your bucket.
demo_settings.cloudflare_worker_checking: Asking the worker whether it can read your bucket.
demo_settings.cloudflare_worker_online: Demos, clips and media are served through Cloudflare.
demo_settings.cloudflare_worker_outdated: This worker was deployed before status checks, so its keys can't be verified. Run the setup again to update it.
demo_settings.cloudflare_worker_keys_rejected: Backblaze rejects the worker's keys, so files that aren't cached yet fail to load. Run the setup again with the keys the panel uses.
demo_settings.cloudflare_worker_misconfigured: The worker is missing its bucket settings. Run the setup again.
demo_settings.cloudflare_worker_bucket_unreachable: The worker can't reach your bucket.
demo_settings.storage_check_description: Writes a test file to your bucket and reads it back, then checks the Cloudflare worker if you use one.
demo_settings.retention_storage_description: Demos are kept at least the minimum retention period. Once total storage exceeds the maximum, the oldest demos past their retention are deleted first.
demo_settings.demo_network_limiter_description: Caps the upload bandwidth a game-server node will use when transferring finished demo files to S3.
demo_settings.clips_retention_storage_description: Highlights are kept at least the minimum retention period. Once total storage exceeds the maximum, the oldest highlights past their retention are deleted first.
demo_settings.clip_video_codec_description: H.264 is the default for the broadest playback compatibility across browsers and devices. H.265 (HEVC) produces ~30% smaller files at matched visual quality and is decoded in hardware by modern Chrome, Edge, Safari, and iOS, but is less universally supported. H.265 falls back to H.264 automatically if the GPU lacks NVENC HEVC.
demo_settings.clip_fps_description: Output frame rate for rendered highlights and manually-edited clips. 60 FPS is smoother but doubles the encode work and file size; 30 FPS is the lighter option.
demo_settings.clip_resolution_description: Output resolution for rendered highlights and manually-edited clips. 1080p balances quality and file size; 720p produces ~50% smaller files. Both benefit when GPU nodes render at 1440p — the streamer supersamples that down to the selected output resolution.
demo_settings.clip_bake_branding: Bake player chip + outro into highlights
demo_settings.clip_bake_branding_description: Renders the player chip overlay and brand outro directly into the highlight file. Disable to ship raw captures without overlays.
demo_settings.auto_generate_match_clips_description: Queue a match-recap highlight for each player after their match finishes.
demo_settings.auto_generate_match_clips_imported_descr: Also auto-generate highlights for matches imported from outside 5stack (e.g. Valve match history). Off by default so imported matches don't flood the render queue.
demo_settings.pause_renders_during_active_match: Pause highlight renders during active match
demo_settings.pause_renders_during_active_match_descri: When a match goes Live on a server backed by a GPU node, auto-pause in-flight highlight renders so the game server isn't competing with the render pod for GPU. Renders resume automatically once the match ends.
demo_settings.auto_clip_always_include_knife_descripti: Append up to 3 knife kills to the end of a player's highlight reel when they got a knife kill — even when their round doesn't meet the minimum-kills filter.
demo_settings.auto_clip_min_kills: Minimum kills to generate a highlight
demo_settings.auto_clip_min_kills_description: Only auto-generate a player's highlight when their best round reached this many kills. Raise it so a match doesn't spawn a clip for everyone.
demo_settings.reparse_warning_title: This reparses every demo — it can take a very long time.
demo_settings.reparse_warning_body: Demos are reprocessed one at a time, which can run for hours or days depending on how many you have. Only do this if you know what you're doing, or after a major update changes how demos are parsed. New stats from updates are reparsed automatically as matches are viewed — this is only to force everything at once.
demo_settings.reparse_confirm_body: This queues a background job that reparses all demos one at a time and can take a very long time. It's not recommended unless you know what you're doing or a major update changed demo parsing. You can cancel it at any point.
demo_settings.reparse_started: Reparse started — it runs in the background, one demo at a time. You can close this page.
demo_settings.reparse_cancel_requested: Cancel requested — stopping after the current demo.
demo_settings.orphaned_dialog_description: Scans the bucket for demo, playback and highlight objects with no matching database row, and corrects the tracked storage sizes. Runs in the background — you can close this dialog and check back.
demo_settings.orphaned_scanning: Scanning… this can take a while. You can safely close this and check back later.
demo_settings.orphaned_no_results: No scan has been run yet.
demo_settings.orphaned_delete_confirm: Permanently delete {count} orphaned object(s) ({size})? This cannot be undone.
demo_settings.orphaned_scan_started: Scan started — this can take a while depending on how many objects you have. You'll get a notification when it's done, so you can close this.
demo_settings.orphaned_tooltip: Find demo, playback and highlight files in S3 that are no longer referenced in the database, and reclaim the space. Runs in the background.

utility.title: Utility
utility.rescan_section_description: Rebuild what the library knows from demos that have already been parsed.
utility.rescan_description: Reads every parsed demo again and rebuilds the mined spots from it. Needed after a parser or miner change — a throw's standing position, for one, is derived differently now. This does not re-parse demos; run that first if they are on an older parser.
utility.callouts_failed: Could not sync the map callouts
utility.library_description: The lineup library: saved throws with where to stand, where to aim and where the utility lands. Turned off, the library is not served and nothing new is taken in.
utility.lineup_daily_limit_description: How many lineups one player may add in a day, counting what the in-game plugin records, what demo mining attributes to them and what they author in the browser. A spam ceiling, not a quota anyone should reach.
utility.practice_description: One-click servers for walking a lineup in. Turned off, the Practice buttons disappear and no session can be started.
utility.practice_connect_minutes_description: How long a booked practice server waits for its host to actually join before it is handed back. This is the cheapest way to hold a server hostage, so it gets a shorter clock than the idle timeout.
utility.practice_max_minutes_description: Only enforced while somebody is queuing for a practice server. With none free and players waiting, a session is ended once it reaches this age; with nobody waiting, a session runs for as long as its host wants.
utility.practice_idle_minutes_description: How long a practice server sits with nobody in it before it shuts itself down. This is for the sessions nobody came back to — it is what keeps an abandoned drill from holding a server all night.
utility.practice_waitlist_minutes_description: How long a player who was turned away still counts as waiting. Nothing serves the queue; it only clears when that player finally gets a server, so an entry that outlives their interest keeps every other session under the maximum-session clock. Lower it if sessions are being cut short with nobody actually waiting.
utility.practice_reserved_servers_description: On-demand server slots practice is never allowed to take. This is the safety valve: with it set, a practice session can never take the last slot out from under a scheduled match. Set it to 0 only if losing a match server to a drill is acceptable.
utility.success_radius_description: How close a throw has to land to the lineup before a drill scores it as a hit. It defaults to 96 source units against a smoke roughly 144 units across, so the default asks the utility to land well inside the smoke rather than merely clipping it. Raise it and mastery comes easier; lower it and only the exact lineup counts.
utility.import_description: Whether lineups may be seeded from a payload rather than recorded in game. An imported lineup is never graded as recorded — nothing here measured it.

drift.title: Utility Drift
drift.subtitle: What a map update did to the lineups already saved on it.
drift.framing: A result says how far a lineup's simulated end point moved between two map revisions. That simulated position means nothing on its own and is never where the utility lands in game, so only the movement and the severity are shown.

reason_notes.start_sealed: The spot you stand on to throw this got walled off by the update. This is the one that actually kills a lineup — the throw cannot be made at all any more.
reason_notes.out_of_world: The flight left the playable space on the new mesh, so there is no end point to compare and no distance to give.
reason_notes.max_flight: The grenade was still travelling when the simulation hit its flight ceiling — usually geometry that used to stop it is gone.
reason_notes.inside_geometry: The flight resolved inside solid world. Rare in practice: a grenade cannot fly into a pocket too small to hold it, so treat this as a scan oddity before you treat it as a dead lineup.

drift.no_distance: No distance: one side of the comparison never resolved, so there is nothing to measure between them.
drift.unsimulatable_note: Either there was no physics seed to replay, or the flight failed on both meshes — and a failure on both says nothing about the update. That is an answer about what could be simulated, not a failed scan, and it says nothing about whether the lineup still works.

accuracy.title: Accuracy (All Shots)
accuracy.description: Out of the total bullets you fired, how many hit an enemy. Volume-dependent — snipers and pistol players fire rarely and hit a high fraction, so this number flatters them. Compare the per-weapon accuracies instead.
accuracy.calculation: All hits divided by all shots, across every weapon.

rifle_accuracy.title: Rifle Accuracy
rifle_accuracy.description: Accuracy with rifles only (AK, M4, AUG, Galil, FAMAS, SG). The fairest aim comparison — rifle vs rifle — since it isn't inflated by low-fire-rate weapons.
rifle_accuracy.calculation: Rifle hits divided by rifle shots. Shown only with at least 5 rifle shots.

pistol_accuracy.title: Pistol Accuracy
pistol_accuracy.description: Accuracy with pistols only (Glock, USP, P250, Deagle, Five-Seven, Tec-9, CZ, Dualies, Revolver).
pistol_accuracy.calculation: Pistol hits divided by pistol shots. Shown only with at least 5 pistol shots.

sniper_accuracy.title: Sniper Accuracy
sniper_accuracy.description: Accuracy with scoped rifles (AWP, SSG, SCAR-20, G3SG1). Naturally high — these are low-volume, one-shot weapons — so judge AWPers against each other.
sniper_accuracy.calculation: Sniper hits divided by sniper shots. Shown only with at least 5 sniper shots.

accuracy_spotted.title: Accuracy (Enemy Spotted)
accuracy_spotted.description: Accuracy when you were actually shooting at an enemy in your field of view. Spam through smoke or walls is excluded.
accuracy_spotted.calculation: Hits on spotted enemies divided by shots fired while an enemy was in vision.

head_accuracy.title: Headshot Accuracy
head_accuracy.description: How many of your hits landed in the head. Excludes shots with AWP.
head_accuracy.calculation: Head hits divided by total hits (AWP excluded from both).

hs_kill_pct.title: HS Kill %
hs_kill_pct.description: Share of your kills that were headshots, as the scoreboard shows.
hs_kill_pct.calculation: Headshot kills divided by total kills.

time_to_damage.title: Time to Damage
time_to_damage.description: Average time from first seeing an enemy to dealing damage to them. Trigger-discipline / hold-angle plays are excluded.
time_to_damage.calculation: Per engagement, time from the rising-edge spot to the first damage on that enemy. Averaged across all engagements; capped at 3s.

spotted_acc.title: Spot Conversion
spotted_acc.description: Of the enemies you spotted, how many you then dealt damage to — an engagement/aggression measure, not aim. (Contrast with Accuracy (Spotted), which is your bullet hit-rate while shooting a visible enemy.)
spotted_acc.calculation: Enemies you spotted and then damaged that round, divided by the total enemies you spotted.

crosshair_placement.title: Crosshair Placement
crosshair_placement.description: Average angle (degrees) your crosshair moved from first seeing the enemy until you hit them. Lower is better.
crosshair_placement.calculation: Per engagement, the angle between your eye direction at the moment of first spot and at the first hit. Outliers above 45° are excluded.

counter_strafing.title: Counter-Strafing
counter_strafing.description: How often you stopped before firing with a rifle. Only counts rifle shots at an enemy in vision; excludes movement while fully crouched.
counter_strafing.calculation: Rifle shots at a spotted enemy where speed was under 34% of the weapon's max, divided by all rifle shots at spotted enemies (not crouched).

first_bullet_accuracy.title: First Bullet Accuracy
first_bullet_accuracy.description: How often your opening shot of an engagement connects — the shot that decides most duels. Higher is better.
first_bullet_accuracy.calculation: First shots that dealt damage divided by first shots fired, across every engagement (one per enemy you opened up on).

tracking.title: Tracking (Time on Target)
tracking.description: While engaging a live enemy, how much of the time your crosshair stayed on them. Higher is better.
tracking.calculation: Frames where your view stayed within ~5° of the enemy, divided by all frames of the engagement window.

spray_accuracy.title: Spray Accuracy
spray_accuracy.description: Your accuracy on the second and later shots of a burst — the shots where recoil matters most.
spray_accuracy.calculation: Hits attributed to spray shots divided by total spray shots. A shot is a spray shot if the same shooter fired within 250ms before it.

wasted_magazine_pct.title: Wasted Magazine %
wasted_magazine_pct.description: How often you reload with bullets still in the magazine. Lower is better — finishing the clip is more efficient.
wasted_magazine_pct.calculation: Bullets left in the mag at each reload, divided by (shots fired + wasted bullets).

trade_kill_opportunities.title: Trade Kill Opportunities
trade_kill_opportunities.description: Rounds where a teammate died while you were alive — i.e. you had a chance to trade.
trade_kill_opportunities.calculation: Distinct rounds in which at least one teammate was killed by an enemy while you were still alive.

trade_kill_attempts.title: Trade Kill Attempts
trade_kill_attempts.description: Enemies you killed shortly after they killed a teammate.
trade_kill_attempts.calculation: Kills against an enemy within 5 seconds of them killing one of your teammates.

trade_kill_pct.title: Trade Kill %
trade_kill_pct.description: How often you converted a trade opportunity into a trade kill.
trade_kill_pct.calculation: Trade kill successes divided by trade kill opportunity rounds.

traded_death_opportunities.title: Traded Death Opportunities
traded_death_opportunities.description: Your enemy deaths — i.e. each death was a chance for a teammate to trade for you.
traded_death_opportunities.calculation: Total times you were killed by an enemy.

traded_death_attempts.title: Traded Death Attempts
traded_death_attempts.description: Total trade attempts your team made on your deaths (a teammate killing your killer within 5s).
traded_death_attempts.calculation: Sum of every teammate kill that traded one of your deaths within 5 seconds.

traded_death_pct.title: Traded Death %
traded_death_pct.description: How often your deaths were avenged by a teammate.
traded_death_pct.calculation: Your deaths a teammate traded within 5 seconds, divided by total deaths.

net_trade.title: Net Trade
net_trade.description: Your contribution to your team's trade balance.
net_trade.calculation: Trade kills you completed minus your untraded deaths.

accuracy_score.label: Accuracy
accuracy_score.coach: Fewer, more deliberate shots land more often than spraying — slow down and commit to each shot.

hs_score.label: Headshots
hs_score.coach: Keep your crosshair at head level as you hold and clear angles so your first shot is a headshot.

spotted_score.label: Spotted Accuracy
spotted_score.coach: Your hit-rate when an enemy is actually visible — pre-aim the spots enemies appear from.

crosshair_score.label: Crosshair Placement
crosshair_score.coach: Hold head-level pre-aim spots so you barely have to move to land the shot.

ttd_score.label: Reaction
ttd_score.coach: Hold tighter angles — the less screen an enemy can appear in, the faster you react and fire.

counter_strafe_score.label: Counter-Strafing
counter_strafe_score.coach: Tap the opposite key to stop dead before firing — shots while moving are wildly inaccurate.

survival_score.label: Survival
survival_score.coach: Trade your life for value — avoid dry-peeking and over-extending away from your team.

traded_score.label: Trade Positioning
traded_score.coach: Fight near teammates so when you die it gets traded, instead of dying for free.

kast_score.label: Round Impact
kast_score.coach: Do something every round — a kill, assist, survive, or get traded. Empty rounds hurt your team.

flash_assists_score.label: Flash Assists
flash_assists_score.coach: Pop-flash for teammates pushing an angle, not just for yourself.

blind_score.label: Flash Effectiveness
blind_score.coach: Throw flashes that actually blind enemies right before a peek — not over their heads.

util_eff_score.label: Utility Damage
util_eff_score.coach: Learn a few HE / molotov line-ups for common spots to get real damage out of each utility.

faq.title: Help & FAQ
faq.intro: How matches and tournaments work here, and what to do when something goes wrong.

what_is.question: What is 5Stack?
what_is.answer: 5Stack is the competition layer for Counter-Strike 2 — the software that sits between a game server and a league. One install runs the whole stack: matchmaking, draft lobbies, teams, tournaments and seasons, stats and Elo, demo capture, in-browser replays, highlights, and live broadcast.

this_site.question: What is {brand}?
this_site.answer: {brand} is a 5Stack instance. The software is open source and self-hosted, so every community that runs it operates its own site, its own servers, and its own rules — this is one of them.

cost.question: Is it free?
cost.answer: Yes. 5Stack is free and open source, and you host it yourself, so there is no per-seat or per-match cost from the project. You pay only for whatever infrastructure you choose to run it on. It is built and maintained by a single developer, and GitHub sponsorships are what keep development going.

sign_in.question: How do I sign in?
sign_in.answer: Through Steam. There is no separate account to create and no password to remember — your Steam profile is your identity here, which is also how matches know who you are once you connect to a server.

games.question: Which games are supported?
games.answer: Counter-Strike 2. The stats, replays, server management, and in-game plugin are all built specifically around it rather than being a generic tournament tool.

find_match.question: How do I get into a match?
find_match.answer: Start from Play. You can queue for matchmaking, which pairs you by region and latency and lets you queue as a party; join a draft lobby, where captains pick teams against a clock; or arrange a scrim through the scrim finder. Which of these are available depends on what this instance has enabled.

check_in.question: Why do I have to check in before a match?
check_in.answer: Check-in confirms everyone is actually at their desk before a server gets reserved and the rest of the lobby is made to wait. Matches with auto-cancellation on show a countdown, and the match is cancelled automatically if the required players haven't checked in by the deadline. In a tournament match, a team that misses the deadline forfeits instead.

tournaments.question: How do I join a tournament?
tournaments.answer: Open the tournament while registration is open and register a team — either one you already have, or a new roster created for that event. Tournaments can run single elimination, double elimination, round robin, or Swiss, and can be chained into multiple stages, with seasonal leagues on top for promotion and relegation.

stats.question: Where do my stats come from?
stats.answer: Every match's demo is parsed after it finishes, so the numbers come from the actual recording rather than from live scoreboard reporting. That gives HLTV rating, KAST, ADR, opening duels, clutches, utility, and per-weapon accuracy, plus Elo movement. The stats guide explains what each figure means and how it's calculated.

replays.question: Can I rewatch a match without downloading the demo?
replays.answer: Yes. Every match has a 2D radar replay and a 3D fly-through that run in the browser, with the round timeline, economy, and kill feed alongside. The raw demo is still downloadable if you want to watch it in CS2 itself.

highlights.question: Where do highlight clips come from?
highlights.answer: Multikills, clutches, and knife rounds are detected automatically when a match ends and rendered into clips. You can also cut your own from any match in the in-app editor. Rendering runs on a GPU node, so clips only appear on instances that have one.

notifications.question: Why can't I turn on push notifications?
notifications.answer: Push is delivered by the installed app rather than a browser tab, so you need to install the app on your device first — the Install button in the menu does this. Once it's installed, the toggle in Settings → Notifications becomes available. On iPhone and iPad this is a hard requirement of the operating system.

self_host.question: Can I run my own instance?
self_host.answer: Yes — that is the intended way to use 5Stack. It is self-hosted and installs with a single command, which brings up Kubernetes (K3s), the database, storage, and the panel itself. The install guide in the docs walks through it end to end.

requirements.question: What do I need to host it?
requirements.answer: A Linux server with at least 3 GB of memory, and a domain you control. Ports 80 and 443 need to be reachable for routing, plus port 8585 for the game server node connector. You'll also point several subdomains at the panel — api, ws, demos, search, and console — so plan for wildcard or per-record DNS.

game_servers.question: Where do the matches actually run?
game_servers.answer: On game server nodes you connect to the panel. You can have it spin servers up on demand, register dedicated hardware you already own, or point at a third-party host. CS2 updates are applied automatically, and regions, Steam Relay, and LAN setups are all supported.

gpu.question: Do I need a GPU?
gpu.answer: Only for the video features. In-browser demo playback, automatic highlight rendering, and live streaming from the panel all render on an NVIDIA GPU node. Everything else — matchmaking, tournaments, stats, the 2D and 3D replays, servers, chat — runs fine without one.

managed.question: Is there a hosted or managed version I can pay for?
managed.answer: No. 5Stack is self-hosted only; there is no SaaS tier or managed offering to buy. 5stack.gg is the maintainer's own public instance, useful for seeing the software running before you install it.

branding.question: Can I make it look like my organization?
branding.answer: Yes. The name, logo, favicon, login page, and the full color theme are all configurable from the admin settings, so an instance reads as your platform rather than as someone else's software with your logo dropped in.

extend.question: Can I extend it with my own code?
extend.answer: In two places. You can embed your own web apps as native panel pages — they inherit the session and design system, so there's no fork to maintain. And on the server side you can run your own CS2 plugins alongside 5Stack's, on either CounterStrikeSharp or SwiftlyS2.

support.title: Still stuck?
support.description: Discord is the fastest route to a human — the people running 5Stack instances are in there. Bugs and feature requests belong on GitHub, and the docs cover installation, servers, and every feature in depth.

rewind.meaning: What the Rounds tab shows when you click a round: that round as it was. Nothing changes until you press Restore.

backup.meaning: What the server saves as each round ends: the score and every player's money, armor and weapons. A restore loads one.

undone.meaning: A round a restore took back. It can come back until the next round ends.

veto.meaning: The teams banning and picking maps, and choosing sides, one step at a time.

fix.where_title: Open It From the Admin Bar
fix.where_1: At the bottom of a match page, press Fix a Problem.
fix.where_2: Pick what went wrong. Each fix opens where it happens: a round fix opens the Rounds tab, a veto fix opens the veto.
fix.steps_1: The list follows the match. Right Now holds the fixes for the step the match is in, and Any Time holds the ones that always work. Nothing is shown greyed out; a line at the bottom says what unlocks later.
fix.steps_veto_caption: During the veto: take back a step, act for a team, or give them more time.
fix.steps_live_caption: While a map is being played: restore a round or start the map over.
fix.who_1: Organizers see it: whoever created the match, the organizers of its tournament, and the site's staff.
fix.who_2: Players don't see it. They can ask for help with
fix.who_3: If you're playing in the match yourself, another organizer has to restore rounds.

restore.pick_1: On the Rounds tab, click the round to play again, on the strip or in the list under it. An amber line marks its start.
restore.pick_2: Rounds after the line are striped: they're the ones that get undone, with a count of the kills and damage that go with them.
restore.pick_caption: Rewinding to the start of round 16 from round 17.
restore.confirm_1: Press {button} in the bar at the bottom.
restore.confirm_2: The server loads the round, and the score goes back with it.
restore.after_1: The match pauses on the restored round so everyone can get ready.
restore.after_2: It carries on once the teams ready up in game. Staff can also press {resume} in the admin bar.
restore.which_live_result: It starts again from its first second. Nothing else changes.
restore.which_earlier_result: Play goes back to the start of that round. The rounds after it are undone, scores and stats included.
restore.which_first_result: There's no backup before round 1, so restart the map instead.
restore.which_note: A round's number is the round you'll play next: restoring round 16 puts both teams at the start of round 16.
restore.wait_1: The game server won't load a round until every player is back on it, so the Restore button waits for them.
restore.wait_2: The bar says who's missing, here {name}. The button unlocks the moment they reconnect.
restore.undo_1: Undone rounds aren't thrown away straight away. Until the next round ends, they wait at the end of the round strip.
restore.undo_2: Picked the wrong round? Press {button} to go forward to where you were.
restore.limit_live: Only while the map is live: not in warmup or the knife round.
restore.limit_over: Not once the map is over. Fix its result instead.
restore.limit_player: Not by an organizer who's playing in the match.
restore.limit_economy: Players in the match don't see the money and weapons preview, so it can't give away the other team's economy.
restore.pick_anywhere: Not on the Rounds tab? Press {fix}, then {round}. It opens there with the round in progress picked.
restore.preview_1: Each player's money, armor and weapons show as they were at the start of that round. Anything different from now is amber.
restore.preview_2: Click another round to move the line, or press Esc to clear it.
restore.preview_caption: {name} isn't connected, so a warning shows beside their name.

restart_map.after: The map goes back to warmup at 0–0. Players stay on the server.
restart_map.undo: The rounds that were played stay on the round strip until the next round ends, so a restart by mistake can be taken back with {link}.

veto.pick_undo: {item} takes back the newest ban, pick or side choice.
veto.pick_mispick: {item} picks the newest step for you. Click any earlier step to go further back.
veto.pick_redo: {item} starts again from the first ban.
veto.step_title: Click the Step That Went Wrong
veto.step_1: Fix a Mis-pick and Redo the Veto open the veto's steps. Click the one that went wrong: it and every step after it are striped.
veto.step_2: The bar names who acts next and lists everything that gets cleared.
veto.confirm_2: The clock starts again for the team whose turn it is.
veto.why_1: Whose turn it is, and whether the step is a ban, a pick or a side, comes from how many steps are done. Take back step 3 and step 4 belongs to someone else, so every step after the one you fix is done again.
veto.why_2: Banned maps go back in the pool, and maps that had been picked come off the match.
veto.more_time: {item} adds time for the team whose turn it is.
veto.more_act: {item} turns on veto override, so you can make the current choice on the veto board for a team that's stuck or has left.
veto.more_after: These fixes stay in Fix a Problem after the veto ends, until the first map goes live. Using one then takes the match back to the veto.

server.reboot: {item} reboots the game server. Players reconnect to the same match.
server.move: To move the match to a different server, pick another one from Fix a Problem.
server.crash: If the server crashed mid-round, reboot it, then restore the round once everyone is back.

results.winner: {item} sets the right winner without playing again.
results.forfeit: {item} ends the match now and gives it to the other team.
results.reparse: {item} reads the demos again. The result stays as it is.

replay.restart: {item} cancels this attempt and opens check-in again for both teams.
replay.tournament: In a tournament, a match that already has a result can be played again with {item}. Standings update.
replay.canceled: A canceled match can be reopened the same way, so it doesn't have to be made again.

tournament.join_1: While registration is open, press **Join Tournament** at the top of the tournament.
tournament.join_2: **As a team**: pick one of your teams, or turn on **Create New Team**.
tournament.join_3: **As a free agent**: press **Sign up**. When registration closes, free agents are drafted into balanced teams, earliest sign-ups first. Anyone left over waits on a waitlist and moves up if a place opens. **Leave pool** takes you out.
tournament.join_4: The organizer decides who can register (teams, free agents, or both), and can make it invite-only or limit it by role or rank.
tournament.roster_1: A lineup is the match type's size (5 for Competitive, 2 for Wingman, 1 for Duel), plus substitutes if the tournament allows them.
tournament.roster_2: The team's owner, captain or team admins add and remove players. They can add players only until registration closes; organizers can still add them after that.
tournament.roster_3: Once the bracket is seeded, a roster can't drop below a full lineup. Add a substitute first, then remove the player.
tournament.roster_4: A player who is needed for a match that hasn't started can't be removed.
tournament.check_1: **Tournament check-in** is on only when the organizer requires it. It opens 60 minutes before the start and closes 15 minutes before, unless the organizer changed that. The organizer decides whether captains, every player, or only organizers check in.
tournament.check_2: Teams that miss it aren't removed, just left out of the bracket. The organizer can let them back in, carry on without them, or give more time.
tournament.check_3: **Match check-in** opens about 15 minutes before each match. Press **Check In** on the match page.
tournament.check_4: If one team doesn't check in by the deadline, it forfeits and the team that did check in wins. If neither team checks in, a coin toss picks the winner, unless the stage uses the Admin match mode: then the organizers decide.
tournament.next_1: On the tournament, the **Bracket** tab shows every match; **Follow a team** highlights yours. The **Matches** tab lists them as Live, Upcoming and Results.
tournament.next_2: Your upcoming matches are also on the Matches page, and you get a notification when check-in opens.
tournament.org_1: Organizers of a tournament are: the person who created it, anyone added under **Manage**, then **Organizers**, members of a team linked to it, and site staff with the tournament organizer or administrator role.
tournament.org_2: Any organizer can add more organizers, pause and resume the tournament, and schedule matches.
tournament.org_3: Opening and closing registration, starting, canceling and resetting the tournament are kept to its creator and to site staff with the tournament organizer or administrator role.
tournament.setup_1: Press **Create Tournament** on the Tournaments page. Each stage is single elimination, double elimination, round robin or Swiss; **Add Another Stage** chains them.
tournament.setup_2: A stage's **Maximum Teams** decides how many teams reach it from the stage before: survivors from an elimination stage, the top of the standings from round robin or Swiss.
tournament.setup_3: Organizers can type a **Seed** for each team before the tournament goes live. Teams without one are seeded at random.
tournament.setup_4: A new tournament is visible only to its organizers until registration opens. Once the bracket is drawn its stages are locked.
tournament.start_1: Press **Open Registration** when teams can sign up, and **Close Registration** to stop.
tournament.start_2: With check-in on, registration closes when check-in ends. Without it, the tournament goes live at its start time.
tournament.start_3: If too few teams have registered by the start time, the tournament is canceled.
tournament.sched_1: Matches start on their own unless **Auto Start** is off or the stage uses manual scheduling. Then click an empty match in the bracket, press **Schedule Match**, and pick a time or **Now**.
tournament.sched_2: With **Negotiated Scheduling**, the two captains agree a time between them.
tournament.sched_3: To change one upcoming match, open its ⋮ menu in the bracket and choose **Match Settings**. This works until the match starts.
tournament.sched_4: Once a stage has matches, its rules are locked for everyone: format, maps, rounds, overtime, timeouts and substitutes. The region, TV delay, check-in and timers can still change.
tournament.results_1: In the bracket, open the match's ⋮ menu and choose **Reset winner**. Pick the right winner, or no winner to play it again, then **Confirm reset**. Later matches that depended on it are cleared.
tournament.results_2: A reset waits while that match, or a later one it feeds, is being played or vetoed.
tournament.results_3: In round robin and Swiss, a result can't be reset once the next stage was seeded from the standings, or once the next Swiss round was paired.
tournament.results_4: On the match page, **Fix a Problem** has the same fixes: the match needs to be played again, the wrong team got the win, or a team can't continue.
tournament.results_5: A canceled match doesn't move the bracket on. Restart it from **Fix a Problem**, or set a winner. If a bracket slot has lost its match, **Recreate Match** appears there.

veto_flow.turns: The teams take turns. Each turn is a ban, a pick or a side choice, and has a clock: when it runs out, the choice is made for that team.
veto_flow.maps: A best of one bans maps until one is left. A series also picks the maps it will play, and the last map left over is the decider.
veto_flow.sides: The team that didn't pick a map chooses its starting side. The decider's sides come from a knife round, when the match has one.
veto_flow.regions: When more than one region is on, the teams veto the region first.
veto_flow.draft: In a draft lobby the veto happens in the draft room. When it ends, the room keeps it up for a few seconds, then sends everyone to the match page, which shows the maps while the server boots. Once the server is ready, the maps fold into their cards and Join Server opens.

operators.body: This site runs on 5Stack, open-source software, and is hosted by its operators. They decide how the site is run and are responsible for the information it holds.

collect.title: What is collected
collect.body: When you sign in with Steam and use the site, it stores:
collect.steam: Your Steam account: Steam ID, profile name, avatar, profile link and country, plus your VAC and game ban status.
collect.gameplay: Your play on this site's servers: match results, stats, kills and positions, utility, ELO, demos and clips.
collect.content: What you add: avatars, team names and logos, other uploads, chat messages, clips and your settings.
collect.social: Your friends, the players you block, and any sanctions on your account.
collect.technical: The session that keeps you signed in, the API keys you create, and your push notification subscriptions with your browser's user agent.
collect.servers: Your IP address, when you join one of this site's community servers.
collect.unregistered: You can have a profile here without ever signing in, for example after joining a server run by this site or appearing in an imported demo. It holds your Steam ID, name and match stats.
collect.uploads: Images are stored as you upload them, including any metadata in the file, such as where a photo was taken.

linked.title: Linked accounts
linked.body: Depending on what this site has turned on and what you choose to connect:
linked.discord: Discord: your Discord user ID, so the site's Discord bot can recognize you.
linked.twitch: Twitch: your Twitch ID, username and display name, and while you're live, your stream's title, game and viewer count.
linked.steam_history: Steam match history: the authentication and share codes you provide, used to import your matches.
linked.steam_presence: Steam presence: if you add the site's Steam bot as a friend, it reads whether you're playing CS2 and your current mode, map and score.
linked.steam_friends: Steam friends: when you ask, your Steam friend list is checked to find friends who play here.
linked.faceit: FACEIT: where the site uses FACEIT, your public FACEIT profile, level and ELO are looked up by your Steam ID.

calls.title: Voice and video
calls.body: Voice and camera streams are sent live to the other people in the call and are never recorded. When a match requires cameras, admins and broadcasters can watch those feeds live.
calls.stun: To connect a call, your browser contacts a STUN server, which sees your IP address. This is Google's server unless the operators run their own.

use.title: How it's used
use.matches: To run matches, lobbies, tournaments and leagues, and to show results and stats.
use.fair_play: To keep play fair and safe: checking Steam bans, applying sanctions and moderating chat.
use.notifications: To send the notifications you've turned on.
use.security: To keep the site secure and working, and to fix problems.

public.title: What others can see
public.body: Your profile is public. Anyone, including visitors who aren't signed in, can see your name, avatar, country, Steam ban status, FACEIT details, match history, stats, teams and tournament results.
public.chat: Chat messages are seen by the people in that room, and staff can review them to moderate.

sharing.title: Sharing with other services
sharing.body: Some information is shared with, or loaded from, other services so the site can work:
sharing.steam: Steam (Valve), to sign you in and read your profile and ban status.
sharing.push: Your browser's push service, such as Google, Apple, Mozilla or Microsoft, which delivers push notifications. They include the sender's name and a preview of the message.
sharing.media: GIPHY when you search for GIFs, and Twitch, YouTube or Kick when you watch an embedded stream. These services see your IP address.
sharing.hosting: The hosting and network providers the operators use to run the site.
sharing.telemetry: The 5Stack project, which receives anonymous totals from this site, such as how many matches and players it has. Nothing in them identifies you.
sharing.law: Information can also be disclosed when the law requires it.

cookies.title: Cookies and local storage
cookies.body: A session cookie keeps you signed in. It lasts 14 days and renews while you use the site. A second cookie remembers whether the sidebar is open. Your browser's local storage keeps preferences such as chat tabs, voice and camera devices, and notices you've dismissed.
cookies.analytics: This site also uses Google Tag Manager, which can load analytics tools that set their own cookies to measure how the site is used.

retention.title: How long it's kept
retention.profile: Your profile, stats and match history are kept until your account is deleted.
retention.chat: Chat rooms expire on timers the operators set, about an hour for matches and lobbies and longer for teams and tournaments. Staff can review match and team chat for 7 days.
retention.direct: Direct messages are kept for a period the operators set, one year by default.
retention.edits: When you edit or delete a chat message, the original text is kept for moderation.
retention.sessions: Community server sessions, including IP addresses, are deleted after 7 days by default.
retention.demos: Demos and clips are removed as storage fills up. The stats taken from them are kept.
retention.backups: Daily backups are kept for 7 days by default.
